requirements.requirement: Planter suitable for sunny kitchen windowsill (compact linear form)
requirements.evidence: 3-cell linear build (pieces at 0,0; 1,0; 0,-1) ~ ~260mm long x 150mm deep; fits windowsill depth. Open bins expose plants to sun.
Three bins filled with soil via fillSoil: bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full-drain, bin:0,-1,0~hex-bin-full, bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-full-drain
Planted basil-young (prop:1), parsley-young (prop:2), mint-young (prop:3) – three distinct herb plugs in soil, staged as harvest-ready young plants

finish.summary: Built a compact 3-cell linear planter with three planted bins (basil, parsley, mint) filled with soil, capped and joint-locked for windowsill use.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

events.text: A sunny kitchen windowsill with three herbs — I'll get your planter ready.
